title: Hotfix: reduce circuit breaker flapping by fixing cooldown + half-open probe gating
author: Christine Wong
description: Context: During the us-east canary rollout of overload protection, we observed breaker state oscillation (closed → open → half-open → open) at ~30–60s intervals for a subset of (model, tier) tuples. This flapping inflated shed rate variance and created noisy alerting, and in a few cases caused routing to alternate between primary and fallback more aggressively than intended. Root cause: the cooldown timer was being reset on transition to HALF_OPEN, which effectively shortened the time the breaker remained open. In addition, half-open probes were not gated by a stable-capacity window; a single successful probe would immediately close the breaker even while the underlying saturation signals were still high, causing rapid re-open. Change summary: (1) Fix cooldown accounting so OPEN duration is measured from OPEN transition, not overwritten by HALF_OPEN entry. (2) Add a minimum-stable window before allowing HALF_OPEN probes (require capacity signals to remain below close thresholds for N seconds). (3) Add a regression test that simulates the canary signal pattern (bursty queue depth + GPU saturation) and asserts the breaker does not transition more than once per cooldown window. Notes: This is a hotfix intended to be safe to backport to the canary config only; behavior is feature-flagged via breaker config defaults, but the bug fix in cooldown bookkeeping is unconditional. Risk: Low-to-moderate; affects transition timing only. Mitigation: Added deterministic unit test + replay-based test using recorded signal series; validated in staging with synthetic overload (perf-canary step traffic) and observed stable OPEN durations. Rollout: land to main, deploy to us-east control plane first, monitor breaker_transition_rate, half_open_probe_rate, shed_rate_p95 for 2 hours, then resume canary expansion per ENG-4834. Metrics to watch: routing.breaker.transition.count (by state), routing.breaker.open.duration, routing.breaker.half_open.probe.allowed/blocked, overload.shed.rate, gateway.overload.errors{code}.
commits: routing/breakers: keep open_since across HALF_OPEN transition (fix cooldown bookkeeping)
routing/breakers: add stable_capacity_window gate for half-open probe eligibility
routing/breakers: rename config fields + document hysteresis semantics
tests: add flapping regression test with recorded saturation waveform
telemetry: emit half-open probe blocked reason + open duration histogram buckets
chore: update default breaker config for canary (stable window = 20s, cooldown = 90s)
conversation: Rafael Mendes: Can you spell out exactly what was resetting the cooldown? I want to make sure we’re not masking a threshold issue with timing changes.

Christine Wong (author): Yep. We store open_until = now + cooldown on OPEN, but we were re-computing open_until on entry to HALF_OPEN as now + cooldown (because HALF_OPEN shares the same struct). That meant OPEN could effectively last as little as 1 probe interval. Fix keeps open_since/open_until set on OPEN transition only; HALF_OPEN no longer mutates it.
Mina Haddad: The stable window gate makes sense, but how do we avoid never probing in chronic partial saturation (e.g., util oscillates)?

Christine Wong (author): The gate is based on the close-threshold signals (queue_depth_p95 and gpu_saturation). If they oscillate, we’ll remain OPEN as intended; probing under unstable conditions is what caused the flapping. If we need more nuance later, we can add a separate probe_threshold distinct from close_threshold, but I wanted the hotfix to be minimal.
Ravi Menon: Please confirm routing won’t spam probes when OPEN. What is probe cadence now?

Christine Wong (author): Probe cadence unchanged (max 1 per probe_interval), and now additionally requires stable_capacity_window to have elapsed. Also added a metric for probe.allowed vs probe.blocked so we can validate in canary.
Peter Holtz: Regression test looks good. One suggestion: assert transition count per (model, tier) is bounded even when signals jitter across the threshold.

Christine Wong (author): Added. The test replays a jittery series and asserts no more than 2 transitions in 3 minutes (OPEN→HALF_OPEN→CLOSED) and never OPEN→HALF_OPEN→OPEN within a single cooldown window.
CI Bot: unit tests failed (flapping_regression.test.ts) - expected transition count <= 2, got 3.
Christine Wong (author): Fixed the test harness to align probe_interval with the simulated clock (was advancing wall clock but not the breaker scheduler tick). Pushed follow-up commit.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. This matches what we saw in the incident channel and should reduce noise. Please coordinate deploy order with oncall.
Mina Haddad: Approved after test fix.
release_notes: Hotfix reduces circuit breaker flapping by correcting cooldown bookkeeping and gating half-open probes on a stable-capacity window; adds regression test and new probe telemetry.
